# cellxgene_measured_genes_v

One row per (gene, CELLxGENE dataset) for every GENCODE v49 gene the dataset measured.
cellxgene_expression_v already uses it to tell 0 from not measured; query it directly to
count how many datasets could have seen a gene. Always filter on chr.

## Scan pruning

Partitioned on `chr`: a literal `chr = <n>` predicate is what keeps a query under the sandbox's per-query scan cap, which BigQuery checks against its partition-pruned estimate before running anything. Clustered on `gene_name`, `gene_id`: an equality on these cuts the bytes actually billed but does not lower that estimate, so it never substitutes for the partition predicate.

## Columns

| column | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chr` | `INT64` | Chromosome (X=23, Y=24, MT=26). Partition column — always filter on it |
| `gene_start` | `INT64` | Gene start (GRCh38) |
| `gene_id` | `STRING` | GENCODE v49 Ensembl gene ID, versioned |
| `gene_name` | `STRING` | GENCODE v49 gene symbol |
| `dataset_key` | `INT64` | Release-local key into cellxgene_datasets_v |
| `dataset_id` | `STRING` | CELLxGENE dataset (stable across versions) |
| `dataset_version_id` | `STRING` | CELLxGENE dataset version |

## Worked examples

Queries that run against cellxgene_measured_genes_v as written.

### How many CELLxGENE datasets measured a gene

```sql
SELECT gene_name, COUNT(DISTINCT dataset_id) AS datasets FROM cellxgene_measured_genes_v WHERE chr = 11 AND gene_name = 'CD3E' GROUP BY gene_name
```
